regime.label: Hot
regime.reading: Housing costs more and is competed for harder than is usual in this city, and has not yet turned.

distress.label: Distress

tape.label: Euribor 12-month
tape.plain: The interest rate most Spanish variable-rate mortgages are priced off. When this rises, monthly repayments follow.

tape.label: ECB mortgage rate (Spain)
tape.plain: The interest rate banks are charging on new mortgages to households, sourced from the ECB's Monetary Interest Rates dataset.

tape.label: Harmonised Consumer Price Index - actual rents
tape.plain: The harmonised index of consumer prices for actual rents on housing, set to 100 in a base year. Shows tenant-cost trend across the Eurozone.

tape.label: Reference rent
tape.plain: What a square metre of rented housing costs per month, from the government's rent index.

tape.label: Appraised housing value
tape.plain: What valuers say a square metre of housing is worth — the number banks lend against.

tape.label: Property transfers (registered)
tape.plain: How many properties were legally transferred, from the land registry. Faster than the price statistics.

tape.label: Registered unemployment
tape.plain: How many people are signed on as unemployed at the job office.

signals.label: Eviction search attention
signals.plain: How often people across Spain look up evictions. Worry and legal research, not evictions themselves.

signals.label: Buy-vs-rent search spread
signals.plain: How often people search to buy compared with to rent. Rising means attention is shifting from renting toward buying.

signals.label: Room-vs-flat search spread
signals.plain: How often people search for a room compared with a whole flat. Rising means households are compressing — taking a room because a flat is out of reach.

signals.label: Foreign interest ratio
signals.plain: Non-Spanish-language Wikipedia views about this city, divided by Spanish-language views — a rising ratio means the world is paying more attention than Spain itself.
signals.note: Computed as (sum of non-Spanish language edition views) ÷ (Spanish Wikipedia views) × 100. A rising ratio signals rising foreign interest; the absolute value is harder to interpret because it depends on platform-wide usage patterns. Used to track whether a city's interest is shifting toward or away from foreign origin markets (relocation, tourism, investment).

signals.label: New vehicle registrations
signals.plain: How many vehicles were newly registered — a fast, keyless read on household and business confidence.
signals.note: Not "new cars sold". Counts DGT transaction code 1 ("Matriculación ordinaria y de ciclomotores") only — genuine new registrations, never transfers of ownership, temporary plates, re-registrations or de-registrations, which are separate transaction codes and excluded. But that transaction code spans nearly every vehicle class, not cars alone: in a sampled month, passenger cars were about 69% of qualifying rows, motorcycles and mopeds about 14%, vans about 9%, and the remainder trucks, buses, trailers, agricultural machinery and a handful of historic and special vehicles. The province is where the registration was filed (DGT's own COD_PROVINCIA_MAT), not the vehicle owner's home province (COD_PROVINCIA_MAT and COD_PROVINCIA_VEH are different fields in the source file) — Madrid runs 3-4x above Barcelona because national fleet, leasing and rental-car operators file their registrations there administratively regardless of where the vehicle will actually operate. That is a real, widely-reported feature of Spanish registration statistics, not a data error: this adapter's province-level annual totals were cross-checked against DGT's own published "Matriculación por provincias" table and matched to within the one month DGT itself never published.

signals.label: Job postings index
signals.plain: Index level of total job postings on Indeed for Spain (100 = February 2020), seasonally adjusted and 7-day lagged. A forward-looking indicator of hiring intent.
signals.note: Indeed publishes daily observations for both 'total postings' and 'new postings'; we use 'total postings'. The index is seasonally adjusted. February 2020 baseline = 100. Recent months are withheld until Indeed's data is complete (before the month ends).

signatures.label: Overheating
signatures.summary: The boom's second act: prices and short-term-rental supply keep climbing while the things that fund them stop. Transactions and permits roll over first, and the storefront churn rate rises before net closures do.

signatures.label: Boom
signatures.summary: People and money arriving faster than the city can house them. Rents and transactions rise together, business formation accelerates, and attention from outside the country runs ahead of the official population count.

signals_against.label: Non-Spanish share of city article views

signatures.label: Distress
signatures.summary: Jobs go first, then the storefronts, then the courts. Foreclosures, evictions and insolvencies rise together while hiring and business formation fall; hardship attention climbs before the judicial series, which are the slowest evidence we have.

signatures.label: Tourism shock
signatures.summary: Visitor demand moves independently of the local economy. Flights, hotel nights and port arrivals turn together while employment and housing lag behind — a shock arriving from outside the city rather than inside it.

signals_against.label: Non-Spanish share of city article views

signatures.label: Orderly cooling
signatures.summary: Heat leaving the market without anyone being forced. Prices and transactions decelerate while employment holds and the distress measures stay flat. This is the benign case, and it is worth being able to name it.

signatures.label: Regulatory shock
signatures.summary: Short-term-rental supply contracts while visitor demand does not. Listings and licensed tourist dwellings fall together with hotel demand steady or rising — the fingerprint of a rule change rather than a demand change.

supply.label: Dwelling stock
supply.plain: How many homes exist in total.
supply.note: Published by province only — there is no municipal breakdown in the ministry's estimate. Madrid province holds about 3.05 million dwellings against roughly 1.5 million in the municipality, so this is provincial context rather than a count of homes in the city. Per-dwelling ratios built on it inherit that scope and are labelled accordingly.
supply.suspect_note: The latest release sits 8.78 median absolute deviations from this measure's recent normal. Treated as provisional — publishers commonly release a partial period first — and kept off the front page until a later release confirms it.

distress.label: Evictions carried out
distress.plain: How many evictions courts actually carried out.
distress.note: Evictions actually carried out, which is the sum of the mortgage, rental-law and other categories CGPJ publishes. It moves separately from eviction orders received, because each court district works through its own enforcement backlog: in the first quarter of 2026, orders received rose sharply almost everywhere while executions fell in Zaragoza and the Balearics and rose in Madrid and Bizkaia. The most recent quarter is provisional and is usually revised upward, so treat it as incomplete rather than as a turning point.
distress.suspect_note: Every city moved sharply the same way in this release, which is far more often a partial period, a definition change or a parsing error than a simultaneous national event. Treated as provisional and kept off the front page until a later release confirms it.
